message.content:
Driving from San Francisco to Los Angeles typically takes around **six to seven hours** under normal conditions—about 380‑400 miles via I‑80 W then I‑580 E into I‑680 S toward I‑5 N, or directly down I‑5 if you’re willing to cross the Bay Bridge first.  

A few things can push that up:

| Factor | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Heavy morning/afternoon rush near the Bay Area or along I‑5 | +30 min – 1 hr |
| Construction / detours | +15–45 min per segment |
| Weather (fog, rain, snow) | +10–20 min |
| Stops (food, gas, restrooms) | +15–30 min |

If you leave early enough to avoid peak congestion, aim for roughly six hours. If you hit heavy traffic or decide to make several stops, plan closer to seven hours.
